advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Include the `audit` nested-dispatch family in `_NESTED_FAMILY` (or otherwise let audit own its children's --help) so `rebar audit serve --help` still renders serve-specific usage.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:40 `_NESTED_FAMILY: frozenset[str] = frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if _BRIDGE_FACTORY is not None and r.parser_factory == _BRIDGE_FACTORY)`
src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:75-77 `if sub in _NESTED_FAMILY: return bool(rest) and rest[0] in ('--help','-h')` else `return wants_help(rest)`
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/audit.py:26 `subs = parser.add_subparsers(dest="subcommand", metavar="{show,serve}")` — audit is a nested family like bridge

src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py:48-49 `if sub in ("show", "serve") and ("--help" in rest[1:] ...): sys.stdout.write(_SERVE_USAGE if sub == "serve" else _USAGE)` — the prior handler served a distinct serve usage that pre_scan now short-circuits
advisory.finding: `rebar audit serve --help` (and any non-leading --help under the audit nested family) now serves the top-level audit.txt via pre_scan instead of the serve-specific usage. _NESTED_FAMILY is derived only from routes sharing the `bridge` parser_factory, so `audit` — which is also a nested subparser (show/serve) whose children owned their own help — is excluded, so help_requested falls through to wants_help and matches --help in any position.
scenarios: `rebar audit serve --help` prints the top-level audit trail help instead of the serve host/port options
advisory.suggested_fix: Derive _NESTED_FAMILY from every nested-subparser factory (bridge AND audit), e.g. add audit's factory, or key off a route flag marking nested-dispatch families rather than only the bridge parser_factory.

The flag is consumed and honored at runtime in reads_cli.main() before the parser factory runs, so the factory-derived help never emits it — narrowing the public help contract without any deprecation note.
scenarios: A user or agent runs `rebar list --help` (or reads docs/cli-reference.md) to discover the --no-pull / offline-read flag and no longer finds it, despite `rebar list --no-pull` still working

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add --check tests that drive the missing-artifact and stray-artifact branches (route present but no .txt; orphan .txt with no route) on an isolated HELP_DIR copy.
evidence: scripts/gen_cli_help.py:162-166 emit distinct `missing artifacts` / `stray artifacts` / `stale artifacts` messages for the three branches
tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py:100-114 `test_check_detects_a_stale_artifact` mutates an existing artifact — exercises only the STALE branch
search of the repo for `stray artifacts` / `missing artifacts` finds only the source strings in scripts/gen_cli_help.py, no test asserting either message or driving a deleted/orphan artifact
ABSENCE: no test adds a new expected route without its .txt (missing) nor drops an unexpected .txt into HELP_DIR (stray) to prove --check catches drift in those directions
advisory.finding: scripts/gen_cli_help.py::_check has three drift branches (missing / stray / stale) and _write deletes stray artifacts, but the test suite exercises only the STALE branch. The missing-artifact branch (a route added without a rendered .txt) and the stray-artifact branch (an orphan .txt for a removed command) — the primary purpose of the --check drift gate — are never driven, so a regression disabling either would pass CI.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror test_check_detects_a_stale_artifact against an isolated sandbox: (a) delete one expected *.txt and assert mod._check() != 0 with 'missing' in stderr; (b) write an extra unexpected *.txt and assert mod._check() != 0 with 'stray' in stderr.
